newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus set to change economic plan, minister says.
newsitem.headline: Belarus set to change economic plan, minister says.

text.p: Belarus's new economic plan, set to take the former Soviet republic to the year 2000, will be changed after criticism from the World Bank and International Monetary Fund, a deputy prime minister said.

"We are being criticised for government interference in the level of the rouble and prices, slow privatisation and strong government regulations," Sergei Ling told a news conference. "We will make changes, but with Belarus's interests in mind."
The 500-page economic plan, approved by hardline President Alexander Lukashenko, forecast inflation rates, deficit figures, unemployment rates and wages to the end of the century.
Ling said Belarus had been forced to print money, regulate the course of the rouble against the dollar, and freeze prices.
He said changes to the Belarus economic programme in line with IMF and World Bank recommendations would take place in late November, when an IMF mission is due to visit Minsk.
The IMF suspended $250 million in credits to the country of 10 million people in January.
Ling said the renewal of a stand-by credit would not be discussed when the mission arrives.
"We understand that we did not meet requirements earlier, mainly in the area of privatisation," said said.
The international funding bodies have told the Belarussian government that they will monitor whether the republic acts on their recommendations in the economic plan.
